# Introduction

The `r Biocpkg("Spectra")` package provides a central infrastructure for Mass
Spectrometry (MS) data in R. The package supports interchangeable use of
different *backends* to represent or import MS data from a variety of formats
and sources (such as mzML files). The *MsBackendMzSpecLib"* package adds support
*mzSpecLib*, a HUPO-PSI formal standard and file format to store and distribute
spectral libraries. This vignette shows how, and which data can be retrieved
from such files.

# Installation

The package can be installed from Bioconductor with:

```{r installation, eval = FALSE}
BiocManager::install("MsBackendMzSpecLib")
```

# General information on the mzSpecLib format

The mzSpecLib format is a community standard of the HUPO-PSI organization for
storing mass spectral libraries. mzSpecLib defines a controlled vocabulary
(CV)-based data model that combines the spectra, metadata (library, spectrum,
analyte, interpretation and peak level) and peak annotations in a single,
extensible format. It supports consensus and predicted spectra, unidentified
spectra grouped in clusters, and spectra with multiple analytes or alternative
interpretations. The data model can be stored in different, inter-convertible
serializations; the specification describes a human-readable plain text format
(`.mzSpecLib.txt`) and a JSON format (`.mzSpecLib.json`).
More information is available at <http://psidev.info/mzSpecLib>.

# Accessing data from mzSpecLib files

The `r Biocpkg("MsBackendMzSpecLib")` package adds support for mzSpecLib
files to `Spectra`-based analysis workflows. Currently the package support only
the *plain text format*, the support to JSON format will be added in th next
versions.

```{r load-library, message = FALSE}
library(MsBackendMzSpecLib)
```

We next load the one of the official mzSpecLib example file which is bundled
within this package using the `Spectra()` constructor function specifying to
use a `MsBackendMzSpecLib` as data backend with parameter `source`.
Other example files can be downloaded from
[mzSpecLib](https://github.com/HUPO-PSI/mzSpecLib).

```{r initialize}
## Get the path/file name of the example file
fl <- system.file("examples", "fetal_brain_tiny.mzspeclib.txt",
                    package = "MsBackendMzSpecLib")

library(Spectra)
sps <- Spectra(fl, source = MsBackendMzSpecLib())
sps
```

We thus have access to all possible spectra variables within a file:

```{r spectra-variables}
spectraVariables(sps)
```

And the full data for spectra variables can be retrieved with `spectraData`:

```{r full-spectra-data}
all <- spectraData(sps)
all
```

The data is organized by individual spectra with a unique integer id. It
is saved in `scanIndex` which identifies each spectrum uniquely within the same
file:

```{r scanIndex}
sps$scanIndex
```

Other than the default `"mz"` and `"intensity"` columns, the full peaks data
can have many more columns, if present, the third one is the `"annotation"`
column, from the fourth can be the personalized ones. The available columns can
be listed using:

```{r peaks-variables}
peaksVariables(sps)
```

To retrieved the full peaks data we use `peaksData`:

```{r peaks-data}
## Request all supported peaks variables
pd <- peaksData(sps, peaksVariables(sps))
## Show the head data for the spectrum number 10
head(pd[[10L]])
```

Below we plot the first 4 spectra.

```{r plot-spectra-frame}
plotSpectra(sps[1:4])
```
